In each case the person made a nondeductible 2025 IRA contribution and converted it, but still had pre-tax money in a rollover IRA on 31 Dec 2025. The tax profile shows no prior IRA basis. Under the pro-rata rule, about 97% of each conversion is taxable.

Five other backdoor Roths (HH-0799, 0608, 1587, 0633, 0747) are clean: those people's pre-tax money sits in 401(k)s, which the pro-rata rule ignores.

### 2025 RMD not met (10)
- **401(k) RMD paid from an IRA (5):** HH-0120, HH-0236, HH-0664, HH-0371 and HH-5271. Each owner turned 73 in 2025. They took one IRA payment sized to cover all three accounts, which matches the 31 Dec 2024 total divided by 26.5 to the cent. A 401(k)'s RMD can't be taken from an IRA, and nothing came out of the 401(k)s before the 1 April 2026 deadline. The missed 401(k) amounts are $12,582.44, $10,955.88, $11,019.74, $15,164.26 and $12,729.96. The five owners who took the 401(k) RMD from the plan itself (HH-0989, 0555, 0637, 0410, 5814) are fine.
- **Inherited IRAs with no 2025 distribution (5):** HH-0607, HH-0842, HH-7126, HH-0466 and HH-0491. In each, the previous custodian confirms the parent had already started RMDs before dying. That makes yearly payments to the beneficiary mandatory from 2025, and none of these five accounts paid out anything in 2025. I didn't calculate the exact RMDs because that needs the IRS Single Life table, which isn't in the files; I list each account's 31 Dec 2024 balance instead. The five inherited IRAs whose original owners died before starting RMDs need no yearly payment.

### Wash sales (4)
In each, a taxable joint account sold at a loss and a spouse's IRA or Roth bought the same fund within 30 days. Because the replacement sits in an IRA or Roth, the washed part of the loss is lost for good rather than added to cost basis.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which households should we call before 15 April 2026 about a 2025 tax or distribution surprise, and why?

Count three kinds of surprise, and no other:
- "backdoor_roth_taxed": a 2025 contribution to a traditional IRA converted to a Roth IRA in 2025, part of which is taxable under the pro-rata rule because the person's traditional IRAs held pre-tax money on 31 December 2025;
- "rmd_not_met": a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any retirement account, that was not met;
- "wash_sale": a 2025 sale at a loss in a taxable account, with the same security acquired within 30 days before or after it in an account of the seller or the seller's spouse, so that some of the loss is a wash sale.

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more households had such a surprise, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
